text:
mika: Quick heads-up — I'm prototyping an attribution explorer for cache token-saved by model / route / customer. Want to fold in kernel-selection and batching experiment tags so we can see what actually changed when perf tweaks land.

jorge: Nice — do you mean a single panel that can compare two time windows + tag filters? :eyes:

mika: Yeah exactly. Two-window diff with absolute tokens-saved and percent delta, plus a breakdown by top-10 tenants and top-10 routes. Also an option to group by kernel variant (eg fused-attn-v2 vs baseline).

anya: Can we also add a warmup cohort slice? i.e., sessions that had <3 warmup hits vs >10. That would help separate warmstart improvements from pure batching gains.

mika: Good call. Plan: build the base panels first then add cohort toggles.

runtime-bot: telemetry snapshot uploaded: /artifacts/cache_attribution/4890123456/summary.tar.gz

jorge: On the query side I'm thinking something like:
```promql
sum by(customer,route,model,tag) (rate(prefix_cache_tokens_saved_total{env="prod"}[1h]))
```
then window diff via Grafana transformations. Thoughts?

dave: For kernel tags we need to make sure the request routing layer propagates kernel_variant and batching_policy as labels. Right now kernel_variant is in logs but not in metrics.

lucy: I'll add a small shim to the metrics exporter to attach kernel_variant and batching_policy tags when present. Should be low overhead.

mika: Awesome. Also we should compute a normalized metric: tokens_saved_per_1k_requests so big customers don't dominate.

anya: SQL for the normalized metric (rough sketch):
```sql
SELECT customer_id, route, model, 
  SUM(tokens_saved) AS tokens_saved, 
  SUM(requests)/NULLIF(SUM(requests)/1000,0) AS requests_per_1k, 
  SUM(tokens_saved)/(SUM(requests)/1000) AS tokens_saved_per_1k_requests
FROM cache_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN $from AND $to
GROUP BY 1,2,3
```

jorge: UX ask: add a small sparkline of per-minute hit-rate next to each tenant row, and a badge if the kernel/batching tag changed inside the window.

dave: For validating causality we should show a scatter: delta in batch size on x, delta in tokens-saved on y, colored by kernel_variant. Quick correlation check.

mika: Agreed. Action list: Jorge -> panel + transformations; Lucy -> metrics tag shim; Dave -> scatter data and kernel tagging validation; Anya -> warmup cohorts and normalized metrics; Mika -> wire sample dashboards and write short runbook for reading attribution.

mika: ETA: base panels by EOD Tue, cohorts + scatter by end of week. Ping me if you need more context.

lucy: Will open PR for exporter change with testcases.

jorge: I'll start with a mocked data dashboard so we can iterate quickly. Putting a draft link in #dashboards when ready.

anya: tiny nit — add a toggle to exclude internal system routes (healthchecks, telemetry) from top lists.

mika: Done. Also adding an opt-in for showing kernel/batching-policy only when sample size > 100 requests to avoid noise.

runtime-bot: experiment label ingestion job completed (304k events).

dave: One more: when we compute percent delta, use smoothed windows (5m rolling) to avoid spiky artifacts from batching bursts.

mika: Yup. We'll include smoothing and a notes panel that lists known experiments overlapping the period.

lucy: PR opened: metrics-exporter#412 — adds kernel_variant + batching_policy labels with unit tests.

mika: Great work team. After initial rollout we'll run the "kernel/batch A/B" workshop with product to interpret the graphs. :rocket:
